judgePersona: Senior engineer who builds and debugs mirage agents daily; impatient with anything between me and root cause. I verified the cited code before scoring: OpRecord (record.py L48-68) genuinely carries source/duration_ms/fingerprint(ETag/md5)/revision(VersionId/SHA)/is_cache, ExecutionNode.records (types.py L39) is computed-then-discarded, the BFF diffs len(ws.ops.records) before/after (server.py L990/L1004-1005) and emits a CUSTOM vfs_op that drops source/duration/fingerprint/revision/tool_call_id (L1406-1411) even though tc_id is in scope ~20 lines up (L1384), the correlateEvents non-breaking last-match loop is the live path (L34-39, wired at RunTracePanel L45-48), RunPage nulls sessionId on workspace switch (L51-53) and passes none of the already-threaded onSelectStep/onHoverStep/highlightedStepId hooks (RunPage L229-236 vs RunTracePanel L23-26/L159-162), and the reusable trace infra (listSessions/getSessionTrace/listTraces/getTrace/TracesView/span metrics) exists and is ignored. Bottom line: feasibility is near-identical across all three (same ~6-line emission fix, same shared risk list), so I discriminate on which PARADIGM gets me to root cause fastest with the least learning tax. I do not reward novelty that adds friction to the common loop, and I dock designs whose headline feature their own risk section quietly admits is partly fiction.

rankings.approach: Mirage Console — Trace Waterfall + Correlated Inspector
rankings.notes: Best fit for the actual daily loop: open the run, click the failing step, see the real bytes — no new mental model. This is the convergent LangSmith/Phoenix/Jaeger/DevTools pattern (tree+waterfall navigation, docked inspector for payloads), so an engineer is productive in seconds; learnability is the highest of the three. It is NOT missing comparison — Compare is a full screen — it just refuses to make comparison the organizing metaphor, which matches reality (most debugging starts with one bad run and no baseline). Mirage-data leverage is strong and concrete: VfsOp lane as the leaf of every exec ToolCall, the fingerprint/revision drift flag ('read v3; current v5') in the inspector, latency-phase bars, effect-class decorations surfaced only when a write touches a system of record. The drift-flag sample interaction is the single clearest articulation across all three of 'this is a data mistake, not a model mistake.' Implementability is the best of the three because the surface is the smallest superset over existing components (RunTracePanel/StepCard/ToolCallRow already exist, the dead hooks are already threaded). Docked at 8/8 on the two data axes only because the headline VfsOp ground-truth card and drift flag are DARK until the L1406-1411 emission fix + from_op_record fix land (verified: source/duration/fingerprint/revision are dropped today), and the Span-metric backbone for the latency phases is still a demo with agent_id='demo-agent' — so the phase bars start as derived estimates. Risk it does not fully escape: a flat waterfall over hundreds of ops needs aggressive virtualization or it becomes a wall of rows. But this is the lowest-risk chassis that still delivers the moat.

Owns the single best NOVEL primitive for finding root cause fast: breakpoint-and-play. 'Set a breakpoint on write-to-system-of-record + fingerprint-drift, hit play at 4x, auto-halt at the exact tick it went wrong, then reverse-step one event' is exactly the rr/reverse-debugger move I reach for in real debugging, and it is only possible because mirage observes the data plane. Breakpoints-as-predicates-over-the-event-stream is the highest-ceiling idea in the whole set and MUST be grafted. Data leverage ties Design 1 for the lead — the World-panel-@-tick-N and the latency-phase scrub push mirage's observability hardest. BUT: making a video-player transport bar the SPINE of the entire product is a learnability tax I will not wave through — engineers expect a tree+inspector they can scan and click, not a timeline they scrub; for the 'I already know it failed at step 9, take me there' case the scrubber is friction, not help. Information density suffers because three time-synced panels over a transport bar leaves less room to scan a long op list than a dense waterfall+inspector. Worst implementability of the three and the most over-promised claim: 'reconstruct the VFS world at tick N' is the headline, yet its OWN risk section admits the backing state of WRITTEN mounts is only 'pinned at stand-up' and not re-derivable per tick — so the marquee World panel is exact only for reads-so-far + overlay and honest-fiction for the rest. Heaviest build (reverse reconstruction, breakpoint engine, lockstep compare). A brilliant MODE to live inside the waterfall, a risky whole-product spine.

Correctly identifies that the highest-value question after 'what did it touch' is 'what CHANGED between the good run and the bad one,' and the 'Data touched' diff (right read customers_2024.csv ETag abc where left read 2023.csv ETag def) is a genuinely killer, uniquely-mirage view that no transcript tool can produce — top-tier data leverage, must graft. The Run Library facets (touched-mount multiselect from vfs_ops.mount_prefix, wrote-to-system-of-record, fingerprint-drift) are the best-specified search surface in the set and directly answer the 'find the leak from last week' JTBD. Investigations-as-saved-evidence (pinned permalinks + verdict: model-vs-data) is the right durability layer. WHY IT RANKS BELOW DESIGN 1: making DIFF the spine is a paradigm mismatch for the most common daily loop — most of the time I am debugging ONE run and have no baseline to diff against, so a comparison-first product makes the 80% case feel like a detour. It also carries the most surface area (Library, Run Detail, Diff, Effects & State, Eval overlay, Investigations = 6 screens) and its OWN risk list names the danger — 'feature sprawl, drifts back toward a tab pile' — which is real here. Its single-run Run Detail is essentially Design 1's waterfall+inspector but second-billed behind the diff machinery, so it pays Design 1's build cost PLUS the diff/notebook cost (hence implementability 6). Information density is high (good), learnability slightly below Design 1 because the pin-and-diff mental model is one extra concept before you can read a single trace. The right move is to take Design 3's diff and Library wholesale and bolt them onto Design 1's chassis, not to invert the priority.

topPick: Mirage Console — Trace Waterfall + Correlated Inspector
bestIdeasToGraft: Design 1's core chassis: Runs index → /runs/:runId waterfall on the Session›Run›Step›{Reasoning|ToolCall}›VfsOp spine → docked Inspector reacting to selection. This is the convergent pattern (LangSmith/Phoenix/Jaeger/DevTools); make it THE default home and lowest-friction path to root cause.

Design 1's VfsOp ground-truth card + drift flag in the inspector: surface source/bytes/duration_ms/mount_prefix/cache-hit/fingerprint(ETag/md5)/revision(VersionId/SHA) per op and flag 'read v3; current v5'. This is THE moat made visible — the clearest 'data mistake vs model mistake' articulation in the set. (Requires the verified L1406-1411 emission fix + from_op_record fix first.)

Design 1's latency-phase-segmented duration bars (model | cache-lookup | byte-fetch | vfs-other) from per-op duration_ms + Span cache_hits/api_calls — nobody else has data-layer phase timing. Click a slow bar → know whether to fix the prompt, the cache, or the data layout.

Design 2's breakpoint-and-play — the single best novel primitive in the entire set. Predicates over the event stream (error, exit_code!=0, write-to-system-of-record, external-effect, fingerprint/revision drift, path glob, bytes>N; policy-deny reserved), Play auto-halts at the first matching tick. Reverse-step backward from there. This belongs in any serious debugger.

Design 2's CausalityBreadcrumb: VfsOp → ToolCall → Step → Reasoning via the stamped tool_call_id, making 'caused-by' visually distinct from 'happened-after'. Jump-to-cause is the answer to 'which reasoning step caused this write?'
Design 2's future-dimming of the waterfall (events after the cursor greyed to ~40%) — a cheap, high-clarity way to show execution position, borrowed straight from step-debuggers.

Design 3's 'Data touched' run diff: diff the real VfsOp set by (op, path) with fingerprint/revision deltas — 'right read customers_2024.csv (ETag abc) where left read 2023.csv (ETag def)'. The killer comparison view no transcript tool can do; the answer to 'what changed between the good run and the bad one.'

Design 3's Run Library facets: touched-mount multiselect (from vfs_ops.mount_prefix), 'wrote-to-system-of-record', 'external-effect fired', 'fingerprint-drift', plus full-text over prompt/command/result/path. Best-specified 'find the run from last week' surface.

Design 3's Investigation/saved-evidence layer: pin runs + step/op permalinks + a verdict (model-mistake vs data-mistake), persisted to the investigations table. Turns ad-hoc spelunking into shareable regression evidence — open a teammate's finding cold at the exact op.

Universal (all three, and correct): real before/after CONTENT diff for every captured write (overlay vs backing), a step scrubber over data-plane state, immutable frozen artifacts with destructive Reset removed from the review path, honest 'SIMULATED — no external system written' labeling instead of a guarded PROMOTE modal, and reserved 'not yet emitted' slots for lineage/policy/credential/PII.
synthesisAdvice:
Ship Design 1 as the chassis and graft Design 2's debugging power and Design 3's comparison/search/durability onto it. Concretely:

(1) DO THE PLUMBING FIRST, IT IS CHEAP AND UNBLOCKS ALL THREE. I verified the fix is a ~6-line edit in one place: in server.py's `for cmd in exec_lines` loop, replace the global before/after diff in `_execute_in_workspace_detailed` (L990/L1004-1005) with `result.tree`'s ExecutionNode.records (already computed and serialized, types.py L39/L51-52), and at the CUSTOM vfs_op emission (L1406-1411) stamp tool_call_id=tc_id (in scope at L1384) plus the dropped source/duration_ms/fingerprint/revision; then fill vfs_ops.tool_call_id in the coalescer. This collapses the three correlation schemes and kills the non-breaking last-match loop in correlateEvents.ts. Until it lands, label op→step attribution 'inferred' everywhere — do NOT repeat the current false-certainty. Two landmines I found that the brief did not name precisely and that must be fixed in the same pass: `_execute_in_workspace_detailed` hardcodes `session_id='default'` to ws.execute() (L991) — a real cross-session correlation bug — and the relay op feed is truncated to `new_records[-20:]` (L1006), which silently drops ops on busy commands. Fix both or the ground-truth promise is a lie on exactly the big runs people most need to debug.

(2) PARADIGM = waterfall+inspector as the spine (Design 1), with Design 2's time-travel as a MODE inside it, not the whole product. Wire the dead onSelectStep/onHoverStep/highlightedStepId hooks (RunPage already gets RunTracePanel which already forwards them — it just passes none). Add a transport/scrubber bar and breakpoints as an optional overlay on the same waterfall, so engineers get the familiar tree by default and the rr-style 'breakpoint, play, halt-at-the-bug, reverse-step' power when they want it — without paying a video-player learning tax for the common 'jump to step 9' case.

(3) MAKE THE RUN A NOUN with Design 3's Library + facets as the home, and keep its Run Diff as a first-class screen (Design 1 also has Compare — adopt the richer Design 3 'Data touched / Reasoning / Tool calls / Cost & gates' diff modes with fingerprint deltas). Comparison is first-class but NOT the spine; single-run debugging is the default.

(4) GOVERNANCE AS DECORATION, NOT CHROME (all three agree, do it): kill the persistent pending-effects counter, the Promote tab, the global LIVE red-chrome, and the typed-PROMOTE modal from the debugging path. Effect-class/reversibility ride on the spine, surfaced only when a write hits a non-scratch class; promote is honestly labeled SIMULATED and physically separated from review. Demote the build-and-branch workspace flow to its own screen (Design 1's move).

(5) HONESTY GUARDRAILS, because the substrate is partial: render cache-hit/'served from cache' as DERIVED (is_cache==ram / absence of network op / Span cache_hits), never as a logged op — cache hits emit no OpRecord. Label the World/state reconstruction as exact for reads-so-far + overlay but 'backing pinned at stand-up' (Design 2's own risk admits this) — do not imply byte-exact full-FS time travel. Show ScoreCard as an overlay joined by run_id with a graceful 'no eval joined' empty state (the FK is convention-only and nothing triggers a sweep). Reserve lineage/policy/credential/PII as visibly 'not yet emitted' panels behind a clearly-labeled section — never fabricate.

(6) DURABILITY: standardize on arcadia_store with pagination/virtualization; do not ship on the 2000-event RAM ring or the localStorage AgentStreamState (verified localStorage-backed) — the review tool's whole premise is that the record survives and is immutable, and large runs will jank or lose data otherwise.

Net: one coherent product is Design 1's tree+inspector + Design 3's Library/diff/Investigations + Design 2's breakpoints/causality/scrub-as-a-mode, all sitting on the single emission fix. That gives the familiar default loop, the killer comparison view, the highest-ceiling reverse-debugging, and the moat (verified bytes at the bottom of the tree) without inventing a new mental model or over-promising state reconstruction.

judgePersona: Information-design / UX critic optimizing for clarity, hierarchy, scannability, and not overwhelming an engineer mid-debug. I verified the load-bearing technical claims against the actual codebase (correlateEvents.ts non-breaking loop, RunPage's dead onSelectStep/onHoverStep/highlightedStepId pass-through, setSessionId(null)-on-switch, hardcoded simulated promote at server.py L2746, the vfs_op emission at L1401-1412 that drops source/duration_ms/fingerprint/revision and never stamps the in-scope tc_id, and the fact that ws.execute() already returns result.tree:ExecutionNode whose per-node .records the BFF discards in favor of len-diffing ws.ops.records). My bias: the run must be a noun, ground truth must be the default home, and the IA must not force a developer to learn a metaphor before they can read a trace. I penalize cleverness that adds cognitive load and reward designs that degrade honestly when the moat backend is dark.

rankings.approach: Mirage Console — Trace Waterfall + Correlated Inspector
rankings.notes: The convergent, correct answer. Span-waterfall + docked detail-inspector is the exact pattern every reference tool (LangSmith/Langfuse/Phoenix/Jaeger/DevTools) settled on, so an engineer needs zero new mental model — the single biggest learnability win in the field. The IA is the cleanest of the three: object-keyed routes (/runs, /runs/:runId, /runs/compare, /workspaces demoted, /live secondary) map 1:1 to the JTBD and to the six critiques without inventing vocabulary. Crucially it scopes the moat correctly: the VfsOp lane is the bottom of the navigation tree and the differentiating fields (source/cache/fingerprint/revision/latency-phase) live in the on-select Inspector — high signal, low resting noise. Implementability is highest because the home view (Runs list + waterfall + inspector + run-switch via listSessions/getSessionTrace + wiring the dead hooks) ships ENTIRELY on shipped data and existing components; the NEEDS-PLUMBING fix only deepens the leaf, it is not a prerequisite for a usable v1. Honest 'simulated' banner and reserved 'not-yet-emitted' slots handled with restraint. Density docked one point: the Trace screen stacks a scrub track, phase-segmented bars, caused-by connectors, effect tags AND a 5-tab inspector — risk of a busy first paint on a large run unless virtualization and progressive disclosure are disciplined. The drift/stale-revision flag in the VfsOp inspector is the sharpest data-correctness feature in any of the three. The spine done plainly and right; the safest center of gravity to build everything else onto.

The most strategically distinctive thesis and the one that best matches the real iteration loop (improve prompt → did it regress?). Its 'Data touched' diff keyed on (op,path) with fingerprint/revision deltas — 'v2 read customers_2024.csv (ETag abc) where v1 read customers_2023.csv (ETag def)' — is the single highest-value feature across all three designs: a data-regression view literally impossible for any transcript-based competitor, and it exploits the moat more pointedly than the generic waterfall. The Investigation object (pinned runs + step permalinks + verdict, backed by the existing investigations table + InvestigationBadges that already exist in the repo) is the best answer to 'turn spelunking into durable, shareable evidence' and reuses real infrastructure. BUT making comparison the spine overreaches: the most common debugging act is reading ONE failing run, and a diff-first product subordinates the 80% case (single-run inspection) to the 20% case (regression diff). That hurts both debugWorkflowFit and learnability — a developer with one bad run shouldn't have to think in terms of pins and a Compare tray. Learnability also suffers from breadth: six primary screens (Library, Detail, Diff, Effects&State, Eval overlay, Investigations) is a tab-pile risk the design itself flags. Implementability docked: the dual synchronized waterfall with step-alignment + git-gutter coloring + four diff modes is substantially more engineering than a single waterfall, and the 'Data touched' diff is only trustworthy AFTER the tool_call_id plumbing lands AND fingerprint/revision are surfaced on every path — so its flagship feature is dark on day one. Excellent ideas; wrong thing chosen as the spine.

The most ambitious and the most evocative exploitation of the moat — and the riskiest as a primary IA. It scores a 10 on leverage because the three-panel 'reasoning | in-flight tool call | reconstructed-world-@-tick-N' with a global scrubber over a GOVERNED DATA PLANE is something no chat-replay tool can touch; breakpoints on fingerprint-drift / write-to-system-of-record + 'play until it breaks, then step backward' is a genuinely novel, debugger-grade idea, and the future-dimming of not-yet-executed steps is a lovely touch. But as the organizing metaphor for the WHOLE product it overwhelms. Time-as-spine forces every user — including the one who just wants to scan a list and read a failed step's stderr — through a transport-bar/tick-cursor model borrowed from rr/Redux DevTools that most agent developers have never used; learnability takes the biggest hit of the three. Information density suffers because three always-on time-synced panels leave little room for dense scanning of hundreds of ops; a flat sortable op table (which Workbench/Waterfall keep) is more scannable for many tasks. Implementability is weakest: the entire value proposition depends on per-tick state reconstruction, which the design's OWN risks admit is exact only for the overlay/reads-so-far — the backing tree of WRITTEN mounts is 'pinned at stand-up' and not re-derivable per tick (matches the verified StatePage deferred-Replay note), so the headline 'rebuild the filesystem at step N' is partially an illusion until snapshots-per-step exist. Reverse-execution UI is also the most expensive surface to build correctly. Verdict: the scrubber and breakpoints are must-graft FEATURES, but time should be a mode inside the waterfall, not the spine of the IA.

topPick: Mirage Console — Trace Waterfall + Correlated Inspector
bestIdeasToGraft: Span-waterfall + on-select docked Inspector as the home view (Waterfall) — the convergent, zero-new-mental-model navigation pattern; the correct skeleton everything else hangs on.

Runs index as the literal home route /runs with full-text search (prompt/command/stdout/path/error) and a touched-mount facet derived from real VfsOp mount_prefix (all three) — the noun that today does not exist; touched-mount search is the moat-powered filter no competitor can offer.

Workbench's 'Data touched' diff mode keyed on (op,path) with fingerprint/revision deltas — the single most differentiating feature in the whole set; 'B read customers_2024.csv (ETag abc) where A read customers_2023.csv (ETag def)' is a data-regression view structurally impossible for transcript tools.

Time Machine's breakpoint-and-play: predicates over the event stream (error / exit_code!=0 / write-to-system-of-record / external-effect / fingerprint-drift / path glob / bytes>N) with Play auto-halting at the first match and stepping backward — debugger-grade and uniquely enabled by ground-truth ops. Ship as a mode, not the spine.

Time Machine's scrub-to-reconstruct cursor over the data plane (rrweb/Redux-DevTools style) + future-step dimming — graft as an OPTIONAL cursor/lens inside the single-run waterfall, honestly scoped to overlay+reads-so-far (label backing 'pinned at stand-up', per the verified StatePage limitation).

Waterfall's drift / stale-revision flag in the VfsOp inspector ('read v3; current v5' via fingerprint/ETag/VersionId) — the sharpest 'data mistake vs model mistake' signal; surface it inline in the inspector AND as a breakpoint predicate.

Per-step latency-phase decomposition (model vs cache-lookup vs byte-fetch) on each duration bar from duration_ms + Span cache_hits/api_calls (all three) — phase-level data-layer timing nobody else has; render cache HITS as explicitly 'derived' since they emit no OpRecord.

Workbench's Investigation object (pinned run/step/op permalinks + markdown notebook + verdict + export), backed by the existing investigations table and InvestigationBadges component already in the repo — turns ad-hoc debugging into durable shareable evidence; lowest-effort high-value graft since the store and badges exist.

Real before/after content diff per captured write (overlay vs backing) replacing the path-list-only OverlayDiff (all three) — with explicit 'preview only / binary / truncated' labeling given VFS reads are string-parsed ls/cat.

ScoreCard as an overlay joined by run_id with 'locate in trace' links from path/op gates (file_exists, ops_must_touch, no_enoent) that set the cursor to the relevant VfsOp (Time Machine's gate→cursor link is the best version) — keeps the execution record immutable; the gate-detail→failing-op jump is a beautiful 'the judge couldn't see it, the VfsOp layer did' moment.

Honest governance treatment shared by all three: kill the persistent pending-counter / Promote tab / global LIVE red-chrome / typed-PROMOTE modal; make effect-class/capture-state/reversibility per-write decorations surfaced only when a write hits a non-scratch class; show a plain 'SIMULATED — no external system written' banner (server.py L2746 is hardcoded simulated) and separate 'review' from any real 'commit'.
Reserved, visibly-labeled 'not yet emitted' slots for lineage/policy/credential/PII (all three) so the IA does not churn when producers land and the tool never fabricates provenance/policy data.
Per-step/per-op permalink into an immutable frozen artifact (/runs/:runId/step/:stepId, /runs/:id#op-:idx, and Time Machine's ?t=:tick) so a teammate opens the exact finding cold.
synthesisAdvice:
Build the Waterfall design as the skeleton, then graft Workbench's diff and Time Machine's time-travel as MODES inside it — do not ship three competing spines. Concretely:

1. ONE IA, object-keyed (take Waterfall's wholesale): /runs (home: searchable, faceted, permalinkable run index with touched-mount facet) → /runs/:runId (single-run waterfall + docked Inspector, the 80% case and the default) → /runs/compare (diff) → /workspaces (the old build-and-branch console, demoted) → /live (relay firehose, secondary). The single-run waterfall is the center of gravity, NOT comparison and NOT a scrubber — that fixes Workbench's and Time Machine's core over-reach while keeping their features.

2. ONE spine, folded: Session›Run›Step›{Reasoning|ToolCall}›VfsOp, with the Span tree, ScoreCard, and relay feed folded on by key. The VfsOp lane is the default bottom of the tree; its differentiating fields (source/cache/fingerprint/revision/latency-phase/effect-class) live in the on-select Inspector so the resting view stays scannable. This discipline keeps density manageable — make ground truth one click deep, not always-on.

3. Diff and Time-travel are LENSES on the same waterfall, reached from a single-run view, sharing all components: a 'Compare' action opens Workbench's dual synchronized waterfall (graft the four diff modes, especially 'Data touched' by op+path with fingerprint/revision deltas, and the DELTA strip from ScoreCards). A 'Scrub' toggle drops Time Machine's tick cursor + future-dimming + breakpoint bar onto the single-run waterfall. Same StepCard/ToolCallRow/VfsOpRow render in all three modes — one component set, three behaviors. This collapses six-screen sprawl (Workbench's flagged risk) and a foreign transport-first metaphor (Time Machine's flagged risk) into one learnable surface.

4. Sequence the build to ship value before the dark backend: (a) v0 on shipped data only — Runs index via listSessions/getSessionTrace, single-run waterfall on existing RunTracePanel/StepCard, WIRE the dead onSelectStep/onHoverStep/highlightedStepId hooks, delete the setSessionId(null)-on-switch and eager createConsoleSession, and label op→step attribution 'inferred' while still using correlateEvents — but FIRST add the missing `break` to fix the non-breaking last-match loop at correlateEvents.ts L34-39 as a one-line correctness patch. (b) Then the linchpin plumbing, stated correctly: in _execute_in_workspace_detailed, consume result.tree (ExecutionNode.records, per-node, walking children for compound `;`/`|` commands) instead of len-diffing ws.ops.records (server.py L990/L1004-1005), and stamp the already-in-scope tc_id plus step_id/run_id AND the dropped source/duration_ms/fingerprint/revision onto each CUSTOM vfs_op at L1401-1412; fill vfs_ops.tool_call_id in the coalescer. Flip the 'inferred' badges to 'correlated' once stamped. (c) Then graft diff, scrubber, breakpoints, ScoreCard overlay, Investigations. (d) Reserve lineage/policy/credential/PII as 'not yet emitted' throughout.

5. Honesty as a cross-cutting principle from all three: ground-truth fields render solid; timestamp-guessed / derived (cache hits) / not-yet-emitted render visibly muted-and-labeled. Replace the path-list OverlayDiff with a real before/after content diff (tolerant of string-parsed VFS reads). Strip the governance theater (pending-counter, Promote tab, LIVE chrome, typed-PROMOTE modal); effect-class becomes a per-write decoration, 'simulated' is labeled plainly, review is separated from commit. Standardize persistence on arcadia_store with pagination so large runs don't truncate mid-scroll/mid-scrub.

Net: Waterfall's skeleton + learnability, Workbench's data-touched diff + Investigation evidence model, Time Machine's scrubber + breakpoints as a mode — one coherent product where the bottom of the tree is verified bytes, the default is reading one run, and comparison/time-travel are a click away rather than a mandatory metaphor.

judgePersona: Pragmatic engineering lead — biases toward what ships on data that exists today, incremental delivery over aspirational scope, and grounds every score in verified codebase reality rather than the brief's framing.
topPick: Mirage Console — Trace Waterfall + Correlated Inspector

rankings.approach: Mirage Console — Trace Waterfall + Correlated Inspector
rankings.notes: Best fit-to-reality of the three. The two scariest-looking pieces are ALREADY in the repo: TraceExplorer.tsx is a complete span waterfall (WaterfallRow depth-indent + duration bars + SpanDetail + orderSpans parent/child ordering, with bytes_read/cache_hits/cache-hit% metrics) — just unrouted; and the cross-highlight hooks (highlightedStepId/onHoverStep/onSelectStep) are already wired end-to-end in InvestigationDetail.tsx L614-627, so RunPage is a *regression*, not a greenfield. The waterfall+detail-inspector-on-select is the convergent industry pattern (LangSmith/Phoenix/Jaeger/DevTools), so learnability is high and the IA won't churn. The five-screen layout (Runs/Trace/Compare/Workspaces-demoted/Live) maps the demoted-workspace decision cleanly onto the critique. Honest scoring caveats keep it off a 9 for implementability: (1) the headline VfsOp leaf is dark until the plumbing fix — switching _execute_in_workspace_detailed (server.py L984) from the len(ws.ops.records) diff to result.tree ExecutionNode.records, stamping tc_id (already in scope at L1384) + source/duration_ms/fingerprint/revision into the CUSTOM value at L1406-1411, and filling vfs_ops.tool_call_id in coalescer L173-179 (currently NULL, and it reads source/duration from a value that is never populated); (2) the span DB that powers rollups/latency-phases is the agent_id='demo-agent' demo with no real session join, so the metric backbone lags the UI; (3) ScoreCardDashboard is keyed to sweep/getAggregate, NOT run_id, so the Eval overlay is new wiring not reuse. The design names every one of these as a risk, which is exactly the discipline I want. Density is good but the 5-tab Inspector (Detail/Effects/Eval/State/Raw) plus phase-segmented bars plus scrub track is a lot to land in v1 — the scrubber and Compare should be deferred, and the design's own risk list concedes the State-tab content diff rides on brittle string-parsed ls/cat.

Strong, and its Investigation screen is the most under-credited asset in the whole brief: InvestigationDetail.tsx already exists, already calls getSessionTrace, already wires the cross-highlight hooks, and the investigations table already exists in arcadia_store — so 'saved debugging session' is half-built, not aspirational. The Run Library + faceted touched-mount search is the correct home and fixes critique #1/#2 squarely. But I'm marking it down on implementability and learnability because its declared SPINE is diff ('diff is the second monitor'), and diff is the single most expensive thing to build well here: it needs (a) the same VfsOp correlation fix as everyone, PLUS (b) reliable cross-run persistence and full-text search that does not exist today (arcadia_store degrades silently to RAM, client state is localStorage), PLUS (c) step-alignment heuristics across two runs whose only tool_name is 'exec' with raw-shell args — aligning 'the good run vs the bad run' by step is genuinely hard when steps aren't semantically labeled. So the product's centerpiece is its riskiest surface, which inverts good incremental sequencing: you'd ship the spine last. The design even flags 'feature sprawl' itself (Library + Detail + Diff + Effects&State + Eval + Investigations = 7 screens) — that's a real v1 scoping problem. Data-touched diff with fingerprint/revision deltas is a genuinely killer, mirage-only capability, but it's a v2 reward gated behind two layers of missing infra. Learnability dips because 'version-control-for-runs' is a less universally-recognized mental model than a trace waterfall for the median agent developer.

The most conceptually exciting and the most thoroughly mirage-native — the three-panel 'reasoning | claimed | actually-did, reconstructed to tick N' is the purest expression of the moat, and breakpoints-on-effect-class/drift is a genuinely novel debugging primitive. I'd happily steal its breakpoint model and its honest cache-hit caveat. But as a *pragmatic* lead scoring buildability on today's data, this is the riskiest of the three and I have to score it that way. The spine IS time-travel, and time-travel over the data plane is the LEAST buildable thing in the whole inventory: (1) the design's own risk #5 concedes that 'reconstruct VFS world @ tick N' is only exact for the overlay/captured-writes — the pre-run backing state of WRITTEN mounts is pinned at stand-up and NOT re-derivable per-tick (StatePage already flags this as deferred), so the headline right-panel is partially un-faithful by construction; (2) before/after content diff rides on string-parsed ls -la/cat (brittle, text-only, no real mtime); (3) cache HITS emit no OpRecord, so the cache-lookup phase and 'served stale from cache' — the literal hero scenario — must be *inferred*, and the whole stale-read story collapses if that inference is wrong; (4) a scrubber needs the FULL immutable event log per run, but events cap at 2000 in RAM and client state is localStorage, so long runs truncate mid-scrub until arcadia_store is the enforced backbone. None of the existing built components (TraceExplorer waterfall, InvestigationDetail hooks) directly accelerate a tick-cursor reducer — it's mostly net-new. Reverse-execution debuggers (rr, Redux DevTools) are also a steeper learnability curve for the median user than a waterfall. High ceiling, low floor; wrong thing to bet the v1 spine on.

bestIdeasToGraft: Approach 2 (Workbench): the saved Investigation as a durable artifact — pinned run/step/op permalinks + markdown notes + a verdict (model-mistake vs data-mistake). This is nearly free to ship because InvestigationDetail.tsx, the cross-highlight wiring, and the arcadia_store investigations table already exist; it converts ad-hoc debugging into shareable regression evidence and is the strongest reuse story in the entire brief.

Approach 2 (Workbench): the touched-mount facet in the run list (filter by /slack, /customers, /finance derived from vfs_ops.mount_prefix). This is a mirage-only filter no transcript tool can offer and is the single most compelling reason to make the Run Library the home screen.

Approach 2 (Workbench): data-touched diff keyed on (op, path) with fingerprint/revision deltas ('right read customers_2024.csv ETag abc where left read customers_2023.csv ETag def'). Defer it to v2, but it is the highest-value differentiating payoff once correlation + persistence land.

Approach 3 (Time Machine): breakpoint predicates over the event stream — halt-on-error, halt-on-write-to-system-of-record, halt-on-fingerprint-drift, halt-on-external-effect. This is a novel, genuinely mirage-native debugging primitive that layers cleanly onto a waterfall (light a notch / auto-scroll-and-select) WITHOUT requiring the full time-travel reconstruction engine.

Approach 3 (Time Machine): the 'future-dimming' affordance — dim everything after the selected cursor to ~40% so you literally see the not-yet-executed steps greyed out. Cheap, and it makes a static waterfall feel navigable like a debugger.

Approach 3 (Time Machine): the explicit, repeated honesty discipline — every inferred value (cache-hit derived from is_cache/Span metric, backing 'pinned at stand-up', correlation 'inferred' when the fallback is used) is labeled rather than faked. This should be a product-wide rule, not one design's nicety.

Approach 1 (Waterfall): latency-phase decomposition on each bar (model | cache-lookup | byte-fetch | vfs-other) from per-op duration_ms + Span cache_hits/api_calls. No competitor has data-layer phase timing; it answers 'fix the prompt, the cache, or the data layout?' directly.

Approach 1 (Waterfall): jump-to-cause from a VfsOp (VfsOp→ToolCall→Step→Reasoning breadcrumb) rendered distinctly from 'happened-after' — causality over chronology, made real by the stamped tool_call_id.

All three: demote the build-and-branch Workspaces surface and strip the global pending-effects counter / LIVE red-chrome / typed-PROMOTE modal; surface effect-class/reversibility as per-write decorations and label simulated promote honestly. This is the correct, unanimous fix to critique #5 and should be non-negotiable in the synthesis.
synthesisAdvice:
Ship Approach 1 (Trace Waterfall + Correlated Inspector) as the product skeleton, because it lands on the two pieces the repo already provides — the working span waterfall in TraceExplorer.tsx and the cross-highlight wiring proven in InvestigationDetail.tsx — and graft the best of 2 and 3 onto it in a deliberate sequence. Concretely:

PHASE 0 — the one fix everything hangs off (do this FIRST, before any UI): rewrite _execute_in_workspace_detailed (server.py L984) to consume result.tree (ExecutionNode.records is the exact per-command op set) instead of the len(ws.ops.records) before/after diff; stamp tc_id (already in scope at L1384) plus source/duration_ms/fingerprint/revision into the CUSTOM vfs_op value (L1406-1411); fill vfs_ops.tool_call_id in coalescer L173-179. This single change collapses the three correlation schemes, kills the non-breaking last-match loop in correlateEvents.ts, and unblocks the VfsOp leaf, jump-to-cause, drift flag, and data-touched diff for ALL later phases. Until it lands, render op→step attribution with an explicit 'inferred' badge.

PHASE 1 — the buildable spine: Runs list as home (wire the already-existing listSessions/getSessionTrace/replayAguiEvents the console currently ignores; delete RunPage's setSessionId(null)-on-switch and eager session-mint). Trace screen = TraceExplorer's waterfall extended with a VfsOp child lane + the now-wired cross-highlight hooks + a docked detail inspector holding untruncated/copyable/searchable args, stdout, AND stderr (fix the 4096 truncation + dropped stderr). Pull in Approach 2's touched-mount facet and Approach 3's future-dimming here — both are cheap and high-value. Demote Workspaces and strip the global promote chrome now, not later.

PHASE 2 — graft the durable artifact: build Approach 2's saved Investigation (pinned run/step/op permalinks + notes + model-vs-data verdict) directly on the existing InvestigationDetail.tsx + investigations table. Add latency-phase bars and the stale-data drift flag from Approach 1. Add Approach 3's breakpoint predicates as a navigation aid over the static waterfall (notch + auto-select), which does NOT require the time-travel engine.

PHASE 3 — the rewards, gated on real infra: ScoreCard overlay joined by run_id (new wiring — ScoreCardDashboard is sweep-keyed today, so reuse its visual primitives, not its data path) and Approach 2's full Run Diff / data-touched diff. These require (a) Phase 0 correlation AND (b) standardizing on arcadia_store with pagination so cross-run search/persistence is real (it degrades silently to RAM today).

DELIBERATELY DEFER (do not let them set the v1 spine): Approach 2's diff-as-spine and Approach 3's full tick-scrubber/world-reconstruction. Both are the most expensive surfaces and both depend on infra that doesn't exist; the scrubber additionally cannot be byte-faithful because written-mount backing is pinned at stand-up and not re-derivable per-tick. Offer a step-cursor that reconstructs overlay/pending-effects (which IS op-by-op derivable) and label backing 'pinned at stand-up' rather than promising full time-travel.

PRODUCT-WIDE RULES from the designs' best instincts: (1) one spine folded, never parallel worlds — Span tree, ScoreCard, relay feed all attach by key; (2) label every inferred/derived/not-yet-emitted value (cache-hits, correlation fallback, lineage/policy/PII slots) instead of faking certainty — adopt Approach 3's honesty discipline globally; (3) immutable frozen artifacts, no destructive Reset on the review path. Net: Approach 1 is the chassis, Approach 2 contributes the home-list facets + saved-investigation + eventual diff, Approach 3 contributes breakpoints + future-dimming + the honesty ethos — sequenced so the buildable-today core ships first and the moat features land as the plumbing catches up.
